questions.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(0,1,1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $n=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨0,\,b,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨1,2,-1⟩=7.$ What is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨1,2,-1⟩=7$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨1,2,-1⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨1,2,-1⟩ & =0 \\ {t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}-{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{3} & ={t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},\,{t}_{2},\,{t}_{1}+2{t}_{2}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{2}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the first component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{1}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{2}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{2}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨0,\,1,\,2⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{b}{c}=\frac{1}{2}.$

questions.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,b,\,0⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,-3⟩=8.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,-3⟩=8$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-1,1,-3⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,1,-3⟩ & =0 \\ -{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}-3{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{2} & ={t}_{1}+3{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{1}+3{t}_{3},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{1},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the third component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{3}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{1}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{1}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{b}=1.$

questions.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-5,-2)$ and is perpendicular to the line 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2-3t \\ y=3+4t \\ z=4-t.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-5,-2⟩.$ Converting the parametric equations of the line to vector form, we get

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2-3t \\ y=3+4t \\ z=4-t\end{aligned}\,⟹\,⟨x,y,z⟩=⟨2,3,4⟩+t\text{ }{{⟨-3,4,-1⟩}_{⏟}}_{v}.
$$

 

The direction vector of the line is $v=⟨-3,4,-1⟩,$ so a normal vector to the plane is 

$$
n=v=⟨-3,4,-1⟩.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ & =⟨3,-5,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-3,4,-1⟩ & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find an equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,-2,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line that goes through the points 
$A(-3,0,2)$ and $B(2,1,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,-2,5⟩.$

Since the line  passes through the points $A(-3,0,2)$ and $B(2,1,3)$ we can find a vector parallel to the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨2,1,3⟩-⟨-3,0,2⟩ \\  & =⟨5,1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨5,1,1⟩.$

Therefore, the equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =⟨3,-2,5⟩\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨5,1,1⟩ & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
